work.title: Les Niais de Sologne
work.movement: With the first and second doubles

version.value: Complete keyboard piece and its two doubles, performed on piano
version.note: The original is for harpsichord. Meyer’s edition is unidentified. The three large sections follow the theme and two doubles; their times are broad passage guideposts.

performers.note: Named in the file attribution and in the discography of the complete Rameau keyboard recordings.

date.note: The two-day session range is documented; the day and take of this individual piece are unspecified.

place.note: Recording venue stated by both sources.

label.note: Label of the collection cited by the uploader.

catalogue.note: The complete Rameau keyboard collection; the Commons file is a single-piece extract.

matrixTakeSides.note: The pressing, runout and take underlying the selected digital file are unidentified.

credits.note: The file credits the collection and uploader; the digitisation engineer is unidentified.

composition.value: Public domain: Rameau’s composition published in 1724
composition.note: Commons applies PD-old-70-expired to the composition. The modern Gouin engraving is consulted as a research source and is not redistributed here.

recording.value: Public domain in the European Union under Commons’ PD-EU-audio designation
recording.note: The host’s licence field is Public domain. Commons separately warns of continuing US protection for this pre-1972 sound recording; the territorial EU designation is not worldwide clearance.

rights.creditLine: Jean-Philippe Rameau, Les Niais de Sologne with two doubles; Marcelle Meyer, piano, Paris, 29–30 October 1953. Les Discophiles Français DF 98/99; Médiathèque musicale Mahler collection; Commons upload by Flopinot2012. Commons PD-EU-audio; US recording restrictions remain.

sources.locator: Les Éditions Outremontaises, 2005, after a facsimile of the 1736 edition. Pages 1, 3, 5 and 7 inspected visually: even-note marking, triplets, left-hand semiquavers and closing reprise.

sources.title: Dictionnaire de l’Académie française — Niais, aise
sources.locator: First edition, 1694, sub-entry under Nid: proverbial niais de Sologne who feigns simplicity and errs to his own advantage.
